classification.classification_note: Stage 01 reproduced an ASan `SEGV` / `wild-addr-read` in `OT::TableRecord::cmp`, but the underlying defect is still an out-of-bounds read from attacker-controlled bytes reinterpreted as a fake OpenType table directory, matching the public CWE-125 report.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42470383 (harfbuzz): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 4 found by fuzz target hb-subset-get-codepoints-fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42470383
bug_description.normalized: The staged 580-byte witness is consumed by `hb_face_create()` as a DFont-like resource fork. Its first 16 bytes decode as big-endian `data_off=256`, `map_off=1`, `data_len=32`, and `map_len=0x20202020`. The resource map bytes at offset 1 yield `typeList=225`, so `type_base` is file offset 226, where the `ArrayOfM1<ResourceTypeRecord>` header stores `lenM1=0x0020`; the first `ResourceTypeRecord` begins at file offset 228 with `tag='sfnt'`, `resCountM1=8224`, and `resourcesZ=288`. Validating 8,225 `ResourceRecord`s from `type_base + 288 = 514` would require 98,700 bytes, far beyond the 580-byte blob. In the vulnerable code `resourcesZ` uses the default nullable `OffsetTo`, so `resourcesZ.sanitize(...)` can neuter that invalid mandatory offset to zero and `sanitize_blob()` can keep the edited blob instead of rejecting it. Later face resolution still sees the same `sfnt` type with count 8225; `get_resource_record(0, ...)` therefore reads element 0 from the null resource-record array, and `ResourceRecord::get_face()` interprets `((data_base+offset).arrayZ)` as an `OpenTypeFontFace`. Because `offset=0` selects the `LArrayOf<HBUINT8>` header at file offset 256, `.arrayZ` starts four bytes later at file offset 260. Those payload bytes begin `20 20 20 20 20 20 00 20`, so the fake face reports `sfnt_version=0x20202020` and `tables.len = 0x2020 = 8224`. `get_table_by_tag()` then binary-searches 8,224 supposed `TableRecord`s, and the first `arr[mid].cmp()` path reads a record far beyond the data block, matching the reproduced AddressSanitizer wild-addr-read in `OT::TableRecord::cmp`. The fix marks `resourcesZ` and the other mandatory DFont offsets as `has_null=false`, so this malformed container is rejected instead of being repaired into a later out-of-bounds read.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that feeds the attacker-controlled blob into HarfBuzz's OpenType sanitizer and stores the accepted result in face state.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 580-byte witness (sha256 `c06ff9d457e74493bb80828cf773b18b9acfe94085ed0bc233bbb785f7c06e27`) used by Stage 01. Its first 16 bytes are `00 00 01 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 00 20 20 20 20 20`, so the blob handed to `sanitize_blob<OT::OpenTypeFontFile>` carries a DFont header with `data_off=256`, `map_off=1`, `data_len=32`, and `map_len=0x20202020`. The same witness later yields `typeList=225` in the map at offset 1; `type_base` is therefore 226, with `ArrayOfM1<ResourceTypeRecord>::lenM1=0x0020` there and the first `sfnt` resource-type entry starting at offset 228 with `resCountM1=8224` and `resourcesZ=288`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The first resource-type entry materializes the witness-controlled count that drives the invalid resource-list validation and later face-selection guard: its bytes are `tag='sfnt'` and `resCountM1=8224`, so this helper returns 8225.
tainted_value_origin.note: These values come from the first `ResourceTypeRecord`, which begins at file offset 228; `type_base` itself is file offset 226 and holds the surrounding `ArrayOfM1` header.

root_cause.description: This field-specific sanitize call treats `resourcesZ` as a nullable offset, so an impossible `ResourceRecord` array can be rewritten to `0` instead of causing DFont sanitization to fail.
root_cause.note: The fixing patch changes this declaration to `OffsetTo<UnsizedArrayOf<ResourceRecord>, HBUINT16, false>`, disabling the `neuter(c)` fallback for this mandatory offset.

sink.description: ASan sink. After the edited resource map reinterprets the 32-byte data block as a fake `OpenTypeFontFace`, this comparison reads the `tag` field from an out-of-range `TableRecord` selected by binary search.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `OT::TableRecord::cmp -> OT::SortedArrayOf<OT::TableRecord, OT::BinSearchHeader>::bsearch -> OT::OffsetTable::find_table_index` with the crash at `src/hb-open-file.hh:58:20`.

parser_admitted.description: The first four witness bytes equal `DFontTag` (`0x00000100`), so HarfBuzz admits the blob as a Mac resource-fork container and enters `ResourceForkHeader` sanitization instead of the regular sfnt/TTC parsers.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness wraps the exact 580-byte witness in `hb_blob_t`, creates a face with `hb_face_create(blob, 0)`, and later calls `hb_face_collect_unicodes(face, output)`.
HarfBuzz sanitizes the blob as `OT::OpenTypeFontFile`; the first four bytes select the DFont path, and resource-fork sanitization reaches the first `sfnt` type entry in the malformed map.
The first `sfnt` type claims 8,225 resources at `resourcesZ=288`; because that offset is incorrectly nullable, vulnerable sanitization can zero the invalid field and still keep the blob.

Later face lookup still uses the edited `sfnt` type for face index 0; `resourcesZ==0` makes resource resolution fall back to `Null(ResourceRecord)`, whose zero data offset selects the `LArrayOf<HBUINT8>` at file offset 256 and recasts its payload at file offset 260 as `OpenTypeFontFace`.
The fake face reports `tables.len=8224`, so table lookup enters binary search over thousands of supposed `TableRecord`s and `OT::TableRecord::cmp` performs the crashing out-of-bounds read.

fine_trace.note: Source. This is the first non-harness project statement that hands the attacker-controlled blob to HarfBuzz's font parser. The staged 580-byte witness begins `00 00 01 00 00 00 00 01 00 00 00 20 20 20 20 20`, so the parser is about to see a DFont header with `data_off=256`, `map_off=1`, `data_len=32`, and `map_len=0x20202020`.
Interpreting the first four bytes as `u.tag` selects `DFontTag`, so the blob enters the Mac resource-fork parser rather than the regular sfnt or TTC paths.

fine_trace.code: return_trace (c->check_struct (this) && data.sanitize (c, this, dataLen) && map.sanitize (c, this, &(this+data)));
fine_trace.note: Using the header bytes from step 1, `data.sanitize` accepts a 32-byte data block at file offset 256, and `map.sanitize` begins parsing a `ResourceMap` at file offset 1 while carrying `data_base = this + 256` into later resource resolution.

fine_trace.code: const void *type_base = &(this+typeList); return_trace (c->check_struct (this) && typeList.sanitize (c, this, type_base, data_base));
fine_trace.note: The map bytes at file offset 1 carry `typeList=225`, so `type_base` becomes file offset 226. `typeList.sanitize` then treats the bytes there as an `ArrayOfM1<ResourceTypeRecord>`: the header at 226 stores `lenM1=0x0020`, and the first `ResourceTypeRecord` begins at file offset 228.

`type_base` points at the `ArrayOfM1` header, but the first `ResourceTypeRecord` begins two bytes later at file offset 228. There the bytes are `tag='sfnt'` and `resCountM1=0x2020`, so this helper returns 8225. That attacker-controlled count drives both the later `idx < type.get_resource_count()` face-selection guard and the attempt to validate a `ResourceRecord` array of that size.

Root cause. For this first `sfnt` type, `resourcesZ=288`, so the resource list would start at file offset 514. Combined with step 5's count 8225, that would require 98,700 bytes of `ResourceRecord`s, which cannot fit in the 580-byte witness. Because `resourcesZ` is declared as the default nullable `OffsetTo<UnsizedArrayOf<ResourceRecord>>`, the called generic `OffsetTo::sanitize` is allowed to replace this invalid mandatory offset with `0` via `neuter(c)`. By source logic, the later crash implies `sanitize_blob()` retried on a writable copy and kept that edited zero offset instead of rejecting the blob.

Later `_hb_face_for_data_reference_table` asks the sanitized blob for face index 0. The first resource type still looks like `sfnt`, and its count is still 8225, so this branch resolves resource 0 through the now-zero `resourcesZ` field from step 6.

With `resourcesZ` edited to `0`, `type_base + resourcesZ` is treated as `Null(UnsizedArrayOf<ResourceRecord>)` instead of the on-disk list at file offset 514. The count is still 8225 and `i` is 0, so this expression returns element 0 from the null array object: a zeroed `Null(ResourceRecord)`.

The `Null(ResourceRecord)` from step 8 has `offset=0`, and `ResourceRecord::offset` is explicitly non-null-safe (`OffsetTo<..., HBUINT24, false>`), so zero selects the start of the data block rather than null. Here `data_base` points to an `LArrayOf<HBUINT8>` at file offset 256, so `(data_base+offset).arrayZ` skips its 4-byte length field and starts at file offset 260. Casting that payload as `OpenTypeFontFace` yields leading bytes `20 20 20 20 20 20 00 20 ...`, hence `sfnt_version=0x20202020` and `tables.len=0x2020 = 8224`.

When the fake face from step 9 is asked for `maxp` during the later `hb_face_collect_unicodes` path, its attacker-controlled `tables.len = 8224` makes this lookup choose binary search instead of the small-table linear search. The saved ASan stack shows this `find_table_index -> bsearch` path immediately under the crash.

With `len = 8224`, the first bsearch iteration sets `min = 0`, `max = 8223`, and `mid = 4111`. `arr = this->arrayZ` points immediately after the fake face header inside the 32-byte data block, so `arr[4111]` is 65,776 bytes past that block. This line therefore forms an out-of-range `TableRecord` reference and passes it to `cmp`.

Sink. The out-of-range `TableRecord` from step 11 is consumed here, and reading its 4-byte `tag` field triggers the saved AddressSanitizer `SEGV on unknown address ... READ` at `src/hb-open-file.hh:58:20`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Not applicable: this sample is an out-of-bounds read and the saved ASan report carries no allocation/free context.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: The saved stack `OT::TableRecord::cmp -> OT::SortedArrayOf<OT::TableRecord, OT::BinSearchHeader>::bsearch -> OT::OffsetTable::find_table_index -> OT::OffsetTable::get_table_by_tag -> _hb_face_for_data_reference_table` matches fine-trace steps 10-12 and the immediate caller that consumes the fake face from steps 7-9.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: The witness-controlled `resCountM1=8224` and `resourcesZ=288` produce the neuter-to-zero at step 6; that zero selects `Null(ResourceRecord)` at step 8, whose non-null-safe zero data offset resolves the `LArrayOf<HBUINT8>` at 256 and casts its payload at 260 as a fake face with `tables.len=8224`, directly driving the crashing binary search.

format.name: malformed DFont resource-fork blob
format.contract: Exactly the staged 580-byte `poc` blob (sha256 `c06ff9d457e74493bb80828cf773b18b9acfe94085ed0bc233bbb785f7c06e27`). It begins with big-endian header fields `data_off=0x00000100`, `map_off=0x00000001`, `data_len=0x00000020`, and `map_len=0x20202020`; the resource map at offset 1 yields `typeList=0x00e1`, so `type_base` is file offset 226 where `ArrayOfM1<ResourceTypeRecord>::lenM1=0x0020`; the first `ResourceTypeRecord` begins at offset 228 and is `sfnt` with `resCountM1=0x2020` and `resourcesZ=0x0120`. The `LArrayOf<HBUINT8>` resource data starts at offset 256, and its payload bytes at offset 260 begin `20 20 20 20 20 20 00 20 ...`. The trigger established here is only this exact witness reaching the vulnerable sanitize/edit path that zeros `resourcesZ`, causing resource index 0 to resolve from that `LArrayOf` payload and later crash during `get_table_by_tag()` table-directory search.
